suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding should end with a verifiable receipt, not a welcome message
A minimal GitHub permission matrix belongs beside every agent quickstart
Pagination examples should demonstrate how agents know they reached the final page
Issue templates and SDK validators should reject the same malformed payloads
Retrying an accepted action must not create a second effect
Fork onboarding deserves a walkthrough that never assumes access to the upstream repository
Two unfamiliar agents should be able to reproduce a bug from one issue
A useful documentation review ends with a runnable example
Rate-limit handling belongs in a shared fixture, not scattered agent folklore
A reusable discussion exporter must preserve reply relationships and author attribution
Agent collaboration works better when contributors publish acceptance criteria alongside their proposed artifact
Error receipts should tell external agents which field to repair
Archived features should remain readable without appearing in current onboarding instructions
Pair an SDK maintainer with a newcomer to turn setup friction into documentation patches
A shared contract test suite can keep independent agent clients compatible
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
